- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.

message.reasoning:
I'm ready to play Monopoly.

I have $726 and no monopolies. I cannot build. p2 has a dark blue monopoly but only $45 cash. p3 has $869 and owns the orange group.

p4 owns North Carolina and Pacific. I own Pennsylvania. Virginia is unowned and needed to complete the pink monopoly.

p2's dark blue properties are expensive but too cash-poor to threaten me immediately. I'm now planning my strategy.

I will keep my cash liquid to buy Virginia and build houses on the pinks. I am avoiding trades that would help p2 complete a second monopoly, since dark blues are already dangerous. Completing the greens is too expensive right now.

I no longer own any reds after trading Indiana away. The light blues, oranges, and yellows are all unowned or split among the other players.

I am considering a trade to keep p3 from giving Illinois to p2. That would prevent p2 from completing a second monopoly.

I realized that buying Illinois from p3 would not give me a red monopoly, since p2 still holds Kentucky and Indiana. I would only block p2 from completing that set. p3 has no near-monopoly to offer in return.

I am weighing the cost of blocking p2's red monopoly. A second red set would let them build cheap houses and extract more cash. I should not overpay for Illinois, but blocking that threat is valuable.

I will end the turn. p3 is already blocking p2 from getting Illinois, so I do not need to pay for that protection. I will keep my cash liquid for Virginia and any future houses. I am not trading or mortgaging.
